blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
The key-value (KV) cache of autoregressive transformers can be viewed
as a fourth-order tensor spanning attention heads, tokens, features,
and grouped layers. We measure the singular-value spectra of all four
mode unfoldings on Mistral-7B-v0.3 and LLaMA-2-13B and compare four
standard tensor decompositions: Tucker, CP, tensor train, and
t-SVD, at matched storage. The spectra partition the four axes into
two classes. The token and feature modes carry low-rank structure,
particularly for keys. The head and layer modes are nearly full-rank
and resist compression at any practical error level. Among the four
decompositions, Tucker achieves the lowest reconstruction error at
every compression ratio from 2 × 2\times to 5 × 5\times , because it can
leave the full-rank modes untouched. Comparisons with two-dimensional
unfolding baselines show that the preferred representation differs
between keys and values: 2D methods achieve lower key error, while
four-way Tucker achieves lower value error at matched storage. A
mode-pinning theorem certifies the full-rank preservation from the
measured spectra alone. Two further spectral properties affect the compressible modes
without touching the full-rank ones: values reach a higher error floor than keys at every
ratio, and post-RoPE keys lose 41 % 41\% – 64 % 64\% of their pre-RoPE
compressibility on both models.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Autoregressive transformers [ 1 ] generate output
tokens one at a time. At each step and each layer, the attention value or output is a weighted combination
of all previous tokens’ value vectors, with weights determined by inner
products between the current token’s query vector and all previous key
vectors. Computing this output therefore requires the key and value
projections of every previous token at every layer. Rather than
recomputing them, inference implementations store them for
reuse [ 2 ] . This stored pair of key and value
matrices is called the key-value (KV) cache . It grows linearly
in the batch size, the context length, the number of layers, and the
number and dimension of the attention heads. Once contexts are long or
batches are large, it is the cache that fills
device memory and limits throughput [ 3 ] .
Low-rank approximations computed via truncated
SVD [ 4 ] are used by existing
methods [ 5 , 6 ] to compress this cache.

blocks.en:
Multi-linear algebra offers several standard tensor decomposition methods to exploit correlations across all of these axes at once [ 4 ] : Tucker [ 7 , 8 ] , CP [ 9 , 10 ] , tensor train [ 11 ] , and t-SVD [ 12 ] .
These decompositions have a long record on the weights of a neural network: convolution kernels have been factored in CP and Tucker form [ 13 , 14 ] and fully connected layers stored as tensor trains [ 15 ] , with the rank of every mode chosen by hand, by a global tolerance or by a per-mode estimator such as VBMF [ 14 ] , rather than allocated under a storage budget.
The KV cache differs from weight tensors as it is regenerated with every new prompt, and the token mode is typically much larger than head mode. Whether the standard decompositions remain effective on the KV Cache tensor has not been structurally studied.
We investigate the compressibility of each tensor mode of the KV cache and compares the reconstruction performance of the four standard tensor decompositions on it. We focus on the multi-linear structure and reconstruction properties.

这些分解器在神经网络的权重上有着很长的记录: 演化内核已经被计入CP和Tucker的形式[13,14],并完全连接的层被存储为拉诺列车[15],其级别为每一种模式由人工选择,由全球容忍度或由VBMF[14]等每模式估计器选择,而不是根据存储预算分配.
KV 缓存与重量分辨器不同,因为它与每个新的快捷符重生成,而符号模式通常比头部模式大得多. 标准分解在 KV 缓存计时器上是否仍然有效, 尚未进行结构研究 。
我们调查KV缓存中每个拉伸模式的可压缩性,比较上面四个标准拉伸分解的重建性能. 我们的重点是多线结构和重建财产。

blocks.en:
We ask that structural question directly.
Which modes of the KV tensor carry compressible structure, which do not, and what does the answer imply for the choice of decomposition?
We extract real caches from two production models, Mistral-7B-v0.3 [ 16 ] , a grouped-query attention [ 17 ] model, and LLaMA-2-13B [ 18 ] , a multi-head attention [ 1 ] model, read off the singular-value spectrum of every mode unfolding, and fit the four decompositions at matched storage across all layers and repeated input draws.
This yields a mode-count dichotomy: the token and feature modes carry compressible low-rank structure, whereas the head and grouped-layer modes are short and exhibit little spectral decay. We call the latter index-like (Definition 3.1 ).

The attention equation above is permutation-invariant: it scores each

blocks.en: Among the evaluated third-order configurations, Tucker gives the lowest error over 2 × 2\times – 5 × 5\times (Section 4 ). We next compare it against two-dimensional factorizations to test whether treating the KV cache as a third-order tensor improves reconstruction. The answer splits on the K/V boundary. On keys, the two-dimensional unfolding has lower error at every ratio tested. On values, full Tucker does. The split holds on both models.

We compare it against Tucker with the head mode pinned at full rank ( r 1 = n h r_{1}=n_{h} ) and the token and feature ranks chosen by the Lagrangian allocator. Both methods use matched storage, averaged over all 32 32 Mistral layers and three prompt draws at T = 1024 T=1024 . Table 4 reports the results.

blocks.en:
The gain does not come from compressing the head axis, which is pinned at full rank throughout. It comes from shared bases. Tucker fits a single token basis and a single feature basis shared across all heads,
so the factor matrices are stored once rather than once per head. Per-head SVD fits
each slice independently and pays the full factor storage cost per head. At matched storage,
this leaves Tucker with a larger rank budget in the token and feature modes.

We now compare Tucker against two cross-layer two-dimensional
factorizations: the grouped low-rank decomposition of
Palu [ 5 ] and the stacked-layer SVD of
xKV [ 6 ] . The Palu-style baseline follows Palu’s grouping of 4 4 adjacent heads and unfolds the head mode into the feature mode to form a ( T , 4 ⋅ d h ) (T,\,4\cdot d_{h}) matrix, but takes a truncated SVD of the cache itself, whereas Palu factors the key and value projection weights offline and caches the resulting latent.
A single truncated SVD per group is taken at a rank
solved from the target compression ratio. xKV unfolds the KV caches of L g = 4 L_{g}=4 adjacent layers into
a single ( T , L g ⋅ n h ⋅ d h ) (T,\,L_{g}\cdot n_{h}\cdot d_{h}) matrix and truncates
its SVD. Tucker is tested in two variants: Tucker-3D takes one

along a fourth mode, matching the xKV and PALU grouping for a controlled comparison, with ranks ( r 1 , r 2 , r 3 , r L ) (r_{1},r_{2},r_{3},r_{L}) . All four
methods use a joint K/V storage budget, pre-RoPE keys,
and are averaged over three prompt draws at T = 1024 T=1024 .

A natural explanation follows from the different roles of the two
weight matrices introduced in Section 2 . The
matrix W V W_{V} produces the value cache that are linearly combined
to form the attention output. To preserve content under arbitrary

approximability. The matrix W K W_{K} produces the key cache whose

directions suffices for this purpose, which leads to rapid spectral
decay and good low-rank approximability. The singular values of the

of W V W_{V} remains comparatively flat ( σ 1 / σ min ≈ 6 \sigma_{1}/\sigma_{\min}\approx 6 ).

blocks.en:
The RoPE operator R R defined in Section 2 rotates
each key and query vector by a position-dependent angle. Because R R applies an independent orthogonal rotation R t R_{t} at each token

budget on the compressible ones.

blocks.en: The authors have followed reproducibility principles valued by the scientific computing community. Code and data that allow readers to reproduce the results in this paper are available at https://github.com/rahulk98/JoLT-Master-Thesis .

blocks.en: AI Use Statement
blocks.zh: AI 使用语句

blocks.en:
The authors used generative AI tools in the following way:
LLM-based coding assistants were used to assist with software implementation; generative AI tools were used to assist with manuscript drafting, and AI-assisted search was used to retrieve related work and to check citation records against publisher metadata. All AI-assisted code and text were reviewed and verified by the authors. The authors take full responsibility for the final content of the paper.
blocks.zh:
作者使用基因AI工具的方式如下:
基于LLM的编码助理用于协助软件的实现;基因AI工具用于协助手稿的起草,AI辅助搜索用于检索相关工作,并对照出版商元数据检查引用记录. 所有AI协助的代码和文本都经过了提交人的审查和核实。 作者对论文的最后内容承担全部责任.
